name: Conf42 Chaos Engineering 2027
description:
###Welcome to Conf42 Chaos Engineering 2027!

This is an **online-only**, 100% remote event streamed on YouTube.

[Conf42](https://conf42.com) events bring together engineers, architects, researchers, and practitioners who enjoy sharing practical experience and real-world knowledge across modern tech stacks. It’s a series of **100% online and pre-recorded events**. 

We have thousand of videos that you can watch for free here: [https://www.youtube.com/@conf42](https://www.youtube.com/@conf42)

For the upcoming Conf42 Chaos Engineering 2027, we are interested in a large variety of topics, especially talks that focus on things people actually build and use:

- New tools, libraries, frameworks, or SDKs, or interesting ways to use existing ones, with clear explanations of where they fit and why they are useful.
- Lessons learned from building, shipping, or running systems, including what went wrong, what worked well, and what you would change next time.
- Architecture and design choices, and how those decisions played out in real-world systems.
- The latest features in platforms, languages, or services, and what they enable in everyday development and operations.
- Performance, scalability, reliability, and tuning work, explained through concrete examples.
- Debugging, testing, observability, and maintenance techniques that made complex systems easier to understand and operate.
- Automation, tooling, and workflow improvements that reduced friction or saved time for teams.
- Security and risk considerations, and how they were handled in practice.
- Case studies and postmortems with practical takeaways others can apply.

Whether your talk is deeply technical or more experience-focused, Conf42 is a place for clear, practical, and honest content. Share what you have learned, pick up new ideas, and help others avoid a few mistakes along the way.

Join a global community of technologists and be part of the conversation shaping how modern systems are built and run.

**We’ll reach out if your talk gets accepted.**

Thank you,
Mark

name: LLMday Montevideo 2026 Q4
description:
### LLM Engineers, assemble in World Trade Center Montevideo, Montevideo on 5 December 2026!

**LLMday** is an in-person event bringing together the fast-growing community of AI researchers, ML engineers, data scientists, and developers working with large language models.

Please note: this is an **in-person-only event**, with no option to present remotely. You’ll need to be present in {location} on {date} in order to deliver your talk.

[Take a look at the lineup so far](https://llmday.com/2026-montevideo-q4/)

#### Who is this for?

- Are you building, fine-tuning, or deploying large language models?
- Do you work on training pipelines, inference infrastructure, or evaluation?
- Are you applying generative AI or agentic systems in real-world scenarios?

If you answered yes to any of these, join us for a day of learning, collaboration, and shared experience.

You will connect with experts shaping the AI landscape, peers exploring what is possible today, and a community that enjoys exchanging ideas, lessons learned, and practical insights.

---

#### Topics

We want to hear about hands-on, experience-driven work across LLMs, AI, and ML, including:

- Lessons learned from real projects, including failures, trade-offs, and surprises.
- Deep dives into model architectures, training workflows, optimization, data, and evaluation.
- Getting started talks that help others adopt LLM technologies more effectively.
- New projects, especially open source tools, frameworks, datasets, or demos.
- Ethics, safety, and responsible AI practices, including bias and alignment.
- Applied AI use cases, integrations, and deployment stories.
- Physical AI, where models interact with hardware, devices, or environments.
- MLOps for LLMs, from experimentation to production.
- Prompt engineering and interaction patterns for models, agents, and systems.

---

#### Am I the right speaker for this?

If you are building, researching, or experimenting with LLMs, the answer is yes.

We welcome speakers from diverse backgrounds across industry, academia, and open source. Whether you work on models, infrastructure, operations, or applications, we are interested in your perspective as long as it aligns with the core themes of LLMs, AI, and ML.

For questions, please ping **mark@llmday.com**.

Thank you for presenting with us!
location: World Trade Center Montevideo - Torre 4, Montevideo

name: SREday Chennai 2026 Q4
description:
### SREs, assemble in Hexaware, Chennai!

**SREday** is a series of in-person events around the world, bringing together the growing communities of Site Reliability Engineers, DevOps practitioners, Platform Engineers, Cloud Architects, CI/CD specialists, and related roles.

Please note: this is an **in-person-only event**, with no option to present remotely. You’ll need to be present in Hexaware, Chennai on 5 December 2026 in order to deliver your talk.

[Take a look at the lineup so far](https://sreday.com/2026-chennai-q4/)

#### Who is this for?

* Are you responsible for the reliability of applications or platforms?
* Do you love systems performance? Do they call you when things 'are slow'?
* Do you make Cloud, Kubernetes and distributed systems work like clockwork?

If you answered yes to any of these questions, join us to learn, network, and share.

You will connect with experts to learn from, peers to learn alongside, and like-minded people to exchange ideas and spend time with.

---

#### Topics

We want to hear about the latest and greatest, including:

- Lessons learned, including real anecdotes and hard-earned insights from things that did not go as planned.
- Deep dives into how systems, tools, or platforms work under the hood, beyond surface-level usage.
- Getting started talks that help others adopt a technology more easily and avoid common early pitfalls.
- New projects, especially open source, with a walkthrough of what you built, why you built it, and how others can get involved.
- Chaos engineering and failure testing, where breaking things on purpose helps ensure systems recover the way you expect.
- Culture and ways of working, including how mindset, collaboration, and operational practices shape reliable systems.

Previous SREday talks, for reference: [youtube.com/@sreday](https://www.youtube.com/@sreday)


Questions? Would you like to bring SREday to your city? - please ping **mark@sreday.com**!

Thank you for presenting with us!

name: PLATFORMday London 2027 Q2
description:
### Platform engineers, assemble in Everyman Canary Wharf, London on 13 May 2027!

**PLATFORMday** is an in-person conference bringing together the people who build and run internal platforms: platform engineering, developer experience, infrastructure, and the tooling that ties them together.

Please note: this is an **in-person-only event**, with no option to present remotely. You’ll need to be present in Everyman Canary Wharf, London on 13 May 2027 in order to deliver your talk.

[Take a look at the lineup so far](https://platformday.com/2027-london-q2/)

#### Who is this for?

- Do you build or operate an internal developer platform?
- Do you work on developer experience, infrastructure, or the golden paths your teams ship on?
- Do you enjoy sharing real experiences, challenges, and opinions about what actually works at scale?

If you answered yes to any of these, join us for a day of learning, discussion, and shared experience.

You will connect with experienced practitioners, peers facing similar challenges, and a community that values honest conversations about the messy reality of platform work.

---

#### Topics

We want to hear about the real world of platform engineering, including:

- Building internal developer platforms, from first golden path to org-wide adoption.
- Developer experience: paved roads, self-service, and measuring whether any of it helped.
- Platform as a product: funding it, staffing it, and proving its value.
- Infrastructure, Kubernetes, and the abstractions teams actually want on top.
- CI/CD, deployment, and the developer inner and outer loop.
- Reliability, security, and cost as platform concerns rather than afterthoughts.
- Honest retrospectives, including the platforms that did not work out.

---

#### Am I the right speaker for this?

If you work on platforms or anywhere around them, then the answer is yes.

We welcome speakers from diverse backgrounds and all walks of life, not just traditional platform roles, but anyone working on developer experience, infrastructure, or operations in a broader sense. We accept a wide range of session types, as long as they align with the core themes of the conference.

Questions? Want to bring PLATFORMday to your city? Please ping **hello@platformday.com**.

Thank you for presenting with us!
